title: Portify Canonical Artifact Manifest
description: Provenance record for a generated canonical artifact (e.g. tokens.json). Schemas are owned by PORTIFY-KNOWLEDGE and are not embedded inline in the distributed artifact files themselves (SCHEMAS_EMBEDDED_IN_DISTRIBUTED_ARTIFACT: NO) — schemaVersion identifies which version of the separately-held schema an artifact was validated against.

artifactVersion.description: Semver of this artifact's own content shape.

schemaVersion.description: Semver of tokens.schema.json (and this manifest.schema.json) that the artifact was validated against.

knowledgeCommit.description: The PORTIFY-KNOWLEDGE commit SHA that last modified every file listed in sourceFiles — NOT necessarily the HEAD commit at generation time. This avoids a self-referential provenance claim (an artifact cannot honestly name the very commit that will contain it) and is deterministic: regenerating from the same source content always yields the same value, regardless of unrelated later commits.

generatedAt.description: ISO 8601 UTC timestamp of this specific generation run. Deliberately excluded from contentHash's input — two generations from identical source content must produce an identical contentHash even though generatedAt differs.

generatorVersion.description: Semver of the generator script itself, so a script defect is distinguishable from a genuine content change.

contentHash.description: sha256 of the exact bytes written to tokens.json, prefixed 'sha256:'. Self-verifying: anyone can independently run `shasum -a 256 tokens.json` and compare to this value without needing to trust or re-run the generator.

domainsIncluded.description: Must exactly match tokens.json's own domainsIncluded field.

sourceFiles.description: Repo-relative paths of every canonical file this generation run actually read. As of Tranche 1A.2 this is normally three files (one per domain's canonical authority: color, radius, spacing), not one — see the generator's own docstring for why a single mockup file is never treated as a runtime authority.

sourceWorktreeClean.description: Must be true. Records that the generator explicitly checked `git status --porcelain` for every file in sourceFiles and found no uncommitted changes before generating — a positive, verified assertion, not merely the absence of a dirty-worktree field. The generator refuses to run (rather than emit this as false) if any source file is dirty.
